title: Comfort, comfort my people
intro: Isaiah 40 marks the beginning of the 'Book of Comfort' (chapters 40–66). After prophecies of judgment, promises of comfort and restoration now follow. The chapter opens with the famous 'Comfort, comfort my people' and contains some of the Bible's most majestic descriptions of God.

items.title: The glory of the Lord is revealed
The nations are like a drop
He who sits above the earth
Lift your eyes to the heights
Those who wait for the Lord
items.note: One of the Bible's most well-known promises

footer.title: A foretaste of the gospel
footer.content: Isaiah 40 is the gospel in Old Testament form: guilt paid, comfort given, God comes as shepherd for his people. The chapter is quoted by New Testament authors as fulfilled in Jesus—he is God's arm revealed, the good shepherd who carries the lambs.
